root_cause.text: In ext4 block allocation, ownership of s_dirtyclusters_counter updates was split between ext4_mb_mark_diskspace_used() and ext4_mb_new_blocks(), causing the same non-delalloc reserved clusters to be decremented twice on the shutdown-triggered error path from ext4_mb_mark_context()/ext4_handle_dirty_metadata().
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit explicitly states “the cause [is] a double decrement in the error path between ext4_mb_mark_diskspace_used() and the caller ext4_mb_new_blocks()”; the patch removes the percpu_counter_sub(&sbi->s_dirtyclusters_counter, reserv_clstrs) from ext4_mb_mark_diskspace_used() and centralizes reservation release in ext4_mb_new_blocks() with “/* release any reserved blocks */ if (reserv_clstrs) percpu_counter_sub(...)”, confirming duplicated counter handling was the bug.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the KUnit test to match the updated ext4_mb_mark_diskspace_used() signature by removing the obsolete third argument.
intent_record.what: The call to ext4_mb_mark_diskspace_used() in test_mark_diskspace_used_range() was updated to remove the third argument, changing it from ext4_mb_mark_diskspace_used(ac, NULL, 0) to ext4_mb_mark_diskspace_used(ac, NULL).
intent_record.how: At runtime, the test now invokes the current two-parameter version of ext4_mb_mark_diskspace_used(), aligning the test with the function's updated interface and allowing it to compile and execute correctly without passing an obsolete extra argument.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the unused or unnecessary `reserv_clstrs` parameter from ext4_mb_mark_diskspace_used to simplify its interface.
intent_record.what: The function signature of ext4_mb_mark_diskspace_used was changed by removing the third parameter, `unsigned int reserv_clstrs`, and placing the remaining two parameters on a single line; no other code in the shown hunk was modified.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this eliminates passing an explicit reservation-cluster argument to ext4_mb_mark_diskspace_used, implying the function will no longer receive that value from callers and must rely on other state or no longer use that input; in the shown hunk itself, no direct behavioral logic change is visible beyond the interface change.

intent_record.intent_summary: Stop ext4_mb_mark_diskspace_used() from incorrectly decrementing the dirty cluster counter for non-delalloc allocations.
intent_record.what: The change removes a comment block and deletes the conditional call that subtracted reserv_clstrs from sbi->s_dirtyclusters_counter when EXT4_MB_DELALLOC_RESERVED was not set in ac->ac_flags, leaving only the subtraction from s_freeclusters_counter before returning.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this stops ext4_mb_mark_diskspace_used() from decreasing the dirty cluster counter for non-delayed-allocation reservations, so dirty cluster accounting is preserved instead of being reduced at this point.

intent_record.intent_summary: Update ext4_mb_new_blocks() to use the revised ext4_mb_mark_diskspace_used() interface by removing the reserv_clstrs argument.
intent_record.what: The call to ext4_mb_mark_diskspace_used() in ext4_mb_new_blocks() was changed from passing three arguments `(ac, handle, reserv_clstrs)` to passing two arguments `(ac, handle)`, removing the `reserv_clstrs` parameter.
intent_record.how: At runtime, ext4_mb_new_blocks() now invokes the updated ext4_mb_mark_diskspace_used() interface without supplying `reserv_clstrs`, so disk space marking no longer depends on that caller-provided argument and instead uses whatever reservation handling is encapsulated inside the callee.

intent_record.intent_summary: Always release reserved cluster accounting on exit from block allocation to avoid leaking dirty-cluster reservations.
intent_record.what: The conditional cleanup block at the `out:` label was changed from only subtracting `reserv_clstrs` from `s_dirtyclusters_counter` when `ar->len` is zero and `EXT4_MB_DELALLOC_RESERVED` is not set, to unconditionally subtracting `reserv_clstrs` whenever it is nonzero, with the old nested checks removed and the comment updated to `release any reserved blocks`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, any reserved cluster count tracked in `reserv_clstrs` is now always released on exit from this path instead of being released only for full allocation failure and non-delalloc cases. This prevents reserved dirty cluster accounting from being left behind in cases where blocks were reserved but not fully consumed under other outcomes or flags, keeping the counter consistent.
